audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer said Ekko on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet read Ekko, Ekko, Ekko, Ekko, Skill, Lux, Lux. Worse, rows 0-3 said Ekko while their whys described Lux chipping him down and winning the trade.
audit.why: Phase Dive (325 range, auto reset) plus the Parallel Convergence stun beats an immobile Lux through the early levels; once Zhonya's is up she stalls the Chronobreak return burst and out-ranges him at 1175/3340.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side = Skill, phases[5..6].side = Lux; phases[0..5].why rewritten so every row's sentence matches its verdict. Content win[0..6] already matched the packet, so no win[] edits were needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] had 3 entries where 4 are expected, and no entry covered the anti-heal timing the missing-interactions file flags.
audit.why: Chronobreak heals Ekko for a percentage of the damage he took in the rewound window, so Grievous Wounds is a real power spike for Lux in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Added spikes[3] for the Oblivion Orb timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three applicable interactions were absent: Chronobreak's healing, Parallel Convergence's shield-on-entry, and Phase Dive being an auto-attack reset whose wind-up is the tell.
audit.why: Riot's text gives all three. Parallel Convergence is 22/20/18/16/14s and 1600 range, arming after a delay; entering it shields Ekko and stuns anyone inside. Phase Dive is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at only 325 range and empowers his next attack. Chronobreak is 110/80/50s and makes him untargetable.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin, dosFull[0], dosFull[1], dontsFull[2] and breakdown.carry now state these with numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT); dosFull[2].d called Chronobreak a "fifteen-second" cooldown.
dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d the tradeBad string, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: The titles asked about wave/ward discipline and about greeding the detonation; the bodies answered neither.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles using Phase Dive's 325 range and Chronobreak's healing.

edits.before: E-poke from max range on his last-hits — the slow zone plus passive auto is your chip engine from level 1.
edits.after: His Timewinder returns through you for a second hit at 1075 units, and you have no dash to leave the field.

edits.before: Q joins: the root threat re-prices every step he takes past the wave's midline.
edits.after: Phase Dive at 325 range is an auto reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-E-auto with the passive detonations is a real chunk. Shield his answer and walk.
edits.after: Parallel Convergence stuns and shields him if he steps into it — never fight on his anomaly.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for his aggression, not yours.
edits.after: His W is 22s at rank 1, so those are the only seconds you get to shove and step up safely.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Final Spark answers his dive, but Chronobreak is 110s of untargetable rewind — land the root first.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes squishies from root range. Force him to dodge or die on every contact.
edits.after: Zhonya's online: stall the Chronobreak return burst, then out-poke him from 1175 units all game.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Chronobreak (R): 110s at rank 1, 50s at rank 3 — he goes untargetable and heals, so hold your last damage until the rewind lands. - Parallel Convergence (W) is 22s and shields him on entry. - Phase Dive (E) is 9s and reaches only 325 units, so he must commit close.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Ekko wins by stunning you on Parallel Convergence, bursting with the Phase Dive reset, and rewinding out on Chronobreak.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by rooting him before Phase Dive closes: at 325 units he has to be inside your E slow, and a rooted Ekko never reaches the rewind.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Chronobreak rewinds him to where he stood seconds ago and heals him — hold Final Spark until after the rewind has resolved.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: A centered wave keeps you outside Phase Dive's 325 units, and a warded flank means Parallel Convergence never blooms behind you.

edits.before: Ekko burns Chronobreak on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Ekko burns Chronobreak on nothing — that is 50 to 110 seconds of free lane.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Holding the detonation at half health is the window Phase Dive wants; and without Grievous Wounds, Chronobreak heals it back.
Chronobreak heals Ekko for a share of the damage he just took, so an early Oblivion Orb decides whether the rewind saves him or not.

notes: The full layer disagreed with content win[] and packet.levelChart on all seven rows; content already matched the packet, so the three side edits are one atomic group and no win[] twins were needed. Rows 0-3 already said Ekko but their whys described Lux winning the trade — those four whys are rewritten here even though the side did not move. Left `ahead`, breakdown.wave, breakdown.late and breakdown.feeding templated: I could not ground an Ekko-specific replacement without inventing. Unverified and therefore not written: whether Prismatic Barrier's shield or Light Binding's root can interrupt Chronobreak's channel, and whether Lucent Singularity's stealth reveal shows the Chronobreak hologram — neither is in Riot's text.
